chapter: New Orleans style and bass playing
title: Tricking musicians who wanted to sit in
summary: Garland and Pops would fool horn players by saying 'follow' and taking them around the keys, including players with A and B clarinets.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: If I have to say myself. I'm pretty fast on that, good on that. I lay dead for that, cause during the days (unintelligible), in the old days, we used to put that on these guys, want to run up and grab a man's instrument and play.

We'd fix him, guy -- Pops can tell you. I jump -- a guy jump up there and want to play, you understand, look over at him and Pops (unintelligible), just stomp, you know, bam-bam-, you know. He say what key? He says, follow. Just follow, and you know what we said, take him around the belt means --
-- start from the first position to seven.

Oh, my God he'd feel, say what key you in, we'd say 'follow.' Never tell the man, you understand this. He play. We'd stop him from coming up there. We dirty, too. Get some -- oh, old those horn players, oh my goodness. Trumpet or a clarinet, you understand, oh, we'd mess them up. We did some -- did some -- you understand, playing -- say, oh, my goodness he couldn't get it at all, you understand --
Well, you know that guy, most the time some of these guys who used to have -- used to carry and A and a B clarinet --
A and B clarinet, set of clarinets.
Oh yes. Every things on one clarinet, nowadays.
Transfer on a B clarinet, but with the A clarinet, course we had to switch clarinets --
Trumpet had to pull out his slide, you know --
